text:
maria: Heads up - saw a sudden jump in 502s on hosted /v1/generate starting ~1745670000. Canary flip to kernel-path-v2 landed ~2m ago. Dash shows ~9% error rate vs 0.3% baseline :grimacing:

sam_oncall: on it. can you share a quick query link?

maria: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/requests?panel=service::/v1/generate - filter by canary=true. errors look gateway-level, 502 + some 504 timeouts.

priya_support: multiple customer tickets coming in about broken responses and timeouts. Customers hitting streaming endpoints get connector resets. Escalating to infra.

sam_oncall: rolling canary weight back to 0 now. `deploy-bot` triggered rollback?

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for deploy kernel-path-v2 -> kernel-path-v1 (canary weight 0). Estimated cutover in 18s. :arrows_counterclockwise:

maria: rollback started but errors persisted for another minute. I think something sticky is keeping traffic pinned to the new runtime instances.

dave_infra: looking at edge routing - we added session-affinity cookie 'rw-stick' in the canary to stabilize long-lived streams. If older nodes don't understand that cookie they may reject or drop the connection.

priya_support: that fits the tickets: customers on long polling sessions see resets while new requests succeed.

sam_oncall: can we reproduce quickly? curl example to hit the gateway: 
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=gpt-open-13b"
```
Run twice, first without cookies then with `rw-stick` from canary.

maria: I pulled an example client report - they had `rw-stick=canary-1` header present and got 502. Without cookie it passed to mainline and worked.

dave_infra: checking proxy logs for cookie routing rule. `kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/proxy-ingress -c proxy -f` shows rejects: 
```
[2025-06-09T18:00:03Z] ERR conn reset: upstream 10.3.4.12:8080 refused stream: unknown kernel-path-v2 handler
[2025-06-09T18:00:04Z] WARN sticky-cookie 'rw-stick' routed to canary pool, upstream unhealthy
```

priya_support: customers reporting billing token errors mixed in - some requests show 401 then 502. Might be unrelated but timeline overlaps.

sam_oncall: hypothesis: canary introduced session-affinity cookie + new kernel that returns 200 for new streams but rejects older tokens or has a mismatch on auth header parsing causing 502 cascade. Steps: 1) Disable affinity cookie at the edge, 2) ensure health checks mark canary unhealthy, 3) rotate connections off canary pool.

dave_infra: disabling affinity now via `edge-config.toggle('sticky_cookies', false)` -> pushed. Also bumped canary health threshold to 90% fail to expedite eviction.

deploy-bot: edge-config update applied. Canary weight set to 0. Health eviction triggered.

maria: errors dropping back to baseline. Grafana shows 502s tailing off. Tickets updated.

priya_support: I posted a note in the customer threads with a brief explanation + apology and status link. Will follow up with impacted accounts for credits.

sam_oncall: quick followups for postmortem: - remove sticky cookie from canary (it shouldn't be global) - add integration test for cookie compatibility with older kernels - add explicit 502->400 mapping when auth header parse fails so proxies don't return gateway errors - add rollout guard to block canary with sticky routing unless all pointer pools opt in.

dave_infra: logging note: make `rw-stick` routing decision and upstream name appear in edge logs for faster triage.

maria: agreed. creating a short incident doc and will attach logs/snippets. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
